title: Separate runtime crypto surface and stage rollback strategy
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Multiple runtime components still link to legacy native crypto bindings (OpenSSL 1.1 shims, native JOSE parser, and an outdated SAML XML verifier). These transitive dependencies expose us to CVE windows and make staged rollouts brittle because of ABI mismatches across distro kernels and our FIPS builds.

Goal: Reduce the runtime's native crypto surface by isolating legacy FFI entry points, providing a thin compatibility shim, and introducing a staged rollback plan so we can land OpenSSL/JWT/SAML upgrades with minimal customer disruption and fast recovery on regression. Work focuses on: identifying direct and transitive dependents, creating a guarded compatibility ABI, adding runtime feature flags, and validating fallback paths (pure-Rust/Go verifiers or hosted verification) for high-risk customers.

Success criteria:
- No customer-facing API changes.
- CI matrix passes across Alpine, Debian, RHEL, and our FIPS artifact image families.
- Rollout can be reverted in <30 minutes for a canary cohort.
- All critical CVEs addressed or mitigated with documented compensating controls.

Scope: code changes in inference-runtime, auth-adapters, and the shared native bindings package; CI matrix updates; canary rollout plan and runbook; performance comparison and telemetry additions to detect regressions.

Out-of-scope: full model-serving kernel rewrites or hardware driver upgrades (handled under other initiatives).
acceptance_criteria: Create compatibility shim that traps legacy FFI calls and routes them to pinned, audited bindings
Add feature-flagged runtime config to opt into new crypto path
CI coverage across four linux families and our FIPS image
Canary rollout to 2% of traffic with automatic rollback on error or latency regression
Documented runbook and postmortem template for any failed rollbacks
test_plan: Unit tests for shim surface and error paths
Integration tests: token issuance/validation, SAML handshake replay, and JWK rotation flows
Performance benchmark: 95th/99th percentile latency before and after on representative inference workloads
Chaos test: inject malformed SAML assertions to ensure graceful failure and monitoring fires
implementation_notes: Step 1: Inventory transitive deps using cargo-udeps / ldd scans on runtime images (ENG-110123 will supply baseline list)
Step 2: Implement lightweight C ABI shim that performs capability checks and returns structured error codes; compile-time gates for FIPS vs non-FIPS
Step 3: Introduce runtime feature flag (REDWOOD_CRYPTO_MODE=shim|native|hosted) and config in operator manifests
Step 4: Build and test pure-managed verifier (rust-jose alternative) as fallback for critical tenants
Step 5: Backport selected patches to the 1.20 runtime branch and validate upgrade path
rollback_plan: Canary-enabled rollout. If canary error rate >1% or latency tail regression >15% vs baseline, GPIO toggle to route canary cohort to previous runtime build. Emergency rollback steps: 1) scale canary target to zero, 2) revert feature-flag in operator config, 3) redeploy previous runtime image, 4) open incident with SRE and notify impacted customers via status page. Documented runbook attached in Confluence (link).
monitoring_and_telemetry: Add telemetry tags for crypto_mode/shim_version in trace spans
Emit token_validation_failure.v1 counter with reason tags
Add 99th percentile latency alert scoped to canary cohort
Add a security-dashboard tile tracking CVE status per artifact
security_mitigation: For bindings that cannot be upgraded in-place, we will ship a compensating mitigation: pinned, signed artifacts with reproducible builds and a runtime integrity check. We will also require SRE manual approval for any canary that includes ABI changes when customer_impact=high.
compliance_notes: Work intersects with FIPS build pipeline. Coordinate with security & compliance to ensure backported OpenSSL builds are validated; record artifacts in internal SBOM registry.
